sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Athens, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Athens-Clarke County Tax Commissioner sends the bill and collects it, while the county's Board of Tax Assessors sets the value. Athens is a consolidated city and county, so one unified government covers the whole of Clarke County except Winterville and part of Bogart, and the same two offices serve every Athens address.

The Tax Commissioner is in Room 250 of the courthouse at 325 East Washington Street, with a mailing address of PO Box 1768, Athens, GA 30603, and a phone line at 706-613-3120. The Assessors' office takes questions about value, appeals and site visits at 706-613-3140. The county notes that the tag office on Lexington Road cannot take property tax payments at its counter, though it has a drop box for checks and money orders.

  • Online lookups and payments go through athensclarketax.com.
  • The county lists a second drop box at the courthouse lower-level entrance.
  • Bills that are not received still have to be paid, since Georgia law has the county mail to the last known address.

sections.h2: When were Athens property taxes due for 2026?
sections.html:
Athens-Clarke County mailed its 2026 bills on August 20, 2026, and payment was due by October 20, 2026. That date has passed, and any balance left open after it accrues interest and penalties.

The county's tax division describes the usual cycle as an October 20 due date for real estate and business personal property. Late balances carry a 5 percent penalty every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a total of 20 percent. Interest also runs on the unpaid amount. The county says Georgia law requires late fees for any bill not paid by the deadline.

Revenue from the bill supports the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County government and the State of Georgia. The county's 2026 budget ordinance sets the general fund rate at 12.25 mills, and a separate 1 mill levy applies to real property in the downtown area under the Downtown Development Authority.

sections.h2: What is the housing market like in Athens for a seller?
sections.html:
Athens is a college town where renters outnumber owners, which changes who buys and what they want. The Census Bureau reports an owner-occupied rate of 40.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, with 53,643 households and a median owner-occupied home value of $299,200. Median gross rent is $1,219.

The University of Georgia anchors the economy, and Athens Technical College adds a second campus. The Clarke County School District serves the city, and private options include Athens Academy and Athens Christian School. Wikipedia places downtown Athens about 70 miles northeast of downtown Atlanta, and lists technology firms and pharmaceutical manufacturers among local employers.

  • The city sits on Piedmont hills, with annual rainfall near 46 inches and about 48 days a year at or below freezing.
  • US 78, US 441 and the SR 10 Loop carry most traffic, and Broad Street and Milledge Avenue cross the city.
  • Census numbers put the city at 128,612 people in 2025, about 1,094 per square mile in the 2020 count.

sections.h2: How do I file a property tax return or appeal in Athens-Clarke County?
sections.html:
Real estate returns go on form PT-50R to the Tax Commissioner in courthouse Room 250 between January 1 and April 1 in any year the property changed hands or was improved. Owners with no changes may skip the return. Missing a required return brings a 10 percent penalty on the unreturned value, plus interest.

Personal property returns, such as business equipment, go to the Board of Assessors every year by April 1. Appeals of a value or an exemption denial go to the Board of Assessors first, and the county says an appeal that ends without agreement is forwarded automatically to the Board of Equalization. The Assessors' office also notes that its staff inspect properties with active building permits, recent sales and open appeals, and that the notice period for those visits runs through December 31, 2026.

Georgia's revenue department sets the filing window at 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice. In Athens that window also controls the homestead deadline, so the same date matters twice.

sections.h2: What homestead exemption does Athens-Clarke County give?
sections.html:
The standard Athens exemption removes $2,000 at the state level, $25,000 from the county maintenance and operations levy and $10,000 from the school levy. Athens-Clarke County says its local exemption for the county portion rose to $25,000 as of 2023.

Owners must own and occupy the home as a primary residence on January 1. Applications are made in person at the Tax Commissioner's office, and the deadline is the same 45-day window used for appeals, typically opening with notices mailed in mid-May. The 2026 application deadline was July 6, 2026. A missed deadline pushes the exemption to the following tax year.

  • Changing the deed, for example by moving the home into a trust or adding a spouse, means applying again.
  • A low-income exemption and several age-based and veteran exemptions exist for qualifying owners.
  • A one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant appears only on the 2026 bill, not on the assessment notice.

sections.h2: What happens to my Athens tax bill if I sell this year?
sections.html:
The bill still goes to the person who owned the home on January 1, even after the property sells. The county's own notice tells new owners to call the Tax Commissioner for payment instructions and tells sellers who received a bill after selling to call so the account does not turn up as delinquent.

The tax division also warns buyers to confirm there are no unpaid taxes before closing, since attorneys check real estate balances but sometimes overlook personal property such as boats or business equipment. A seller who is behind should request a payoff figure from the office on 706-613-3120 and bring it to the closing table so the title company can pay it from proceeds.

Georgia's revenue department adds that no refund is available for a partial year of ownership. Unpaid taxes that reach the collection stage can lead to levy and sale of the property, according to the county's tax division. Selling before that point keeps the sale in your control and the balance in the closing statement.

faqs.q: How much is the Athens-Clarke County millage rate?
faqs.a: The 2026 budget ordinance sets the general fund rate at 12.25 mills for Athens-Clarke County government. Downtown real property carries an extra 1 mill levy, and school and state levies are billed separately on the same statement.

faqs.q: Where can I mail an Athens property tax payment?
faqs.a: Mail it to the Tax Commissioner at PO Box 1768, Athens, GA 30603. You can also pay online at athensclarketax.com, in person in courthouse Room 250 or in a drop box, using checks or money orders only in the drop box.

faqs.q: Did the 2026 Athens bill include any one-time credit?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says a one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant is applied to 2026 bills for each qualifying homestead. It shows up on the tax bill, not on the assessment notice, so do not look for it on the notice.

faqs.q: Do I need a new homestead application if I add someone to the deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says an approved exemption stays in place while you own and occupy the home, but a change in ownership, such as adding a spouse to the deed or moving the home into a trust, requires a new application.

faqs.q: Who do I call about an Athens property value I disagree with?
faqs.a: Call the Athens-Clarke County Board of Assessors at 706-613-3140 and file a written appeal within 45 days of the notice date. If no agreement is reached, the appeal goes to the Board of Equalization.
